title: Tag query parser and note index
instructions:
Build a note index with AND/OR tag queries, split across two modules.

## Files
- `tag_query.py`
- `note_index.py`

In `tag_query.py`:
- `normalize_tag(tag) -> str`: strip outer whitespace, lowercase, then require
  ASCII `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*`; invalid strings raise `ValueError`. Inputs are strings.
- `parse_query(query) -> tuple[list[frozenset[str]], frozenset[str]]`: split on
  whitespace. A positive token is one tag or several tags joined by `|` (OR).
  Each positive token adds a frozenset to the list, preserving token order.
  A token starting with `-` excludes a single tag (no `|` allowed). Return positive
  groups and a frozenset of excluded tags. Normalize tags, collapse duplicates
  within each group/exclusion set, but keep repeated positive groups. Empty query
  gives `([], frozenset())`. Empty alternatives, bare `-`, and invalid tags raise
  `ValueError`. No quoted strings, parentheses, or spaces inside an OR token.
  Example `Work|HOME urgent -Archived` means (work OR home) AND urgent AND NOT archived.

In `note_index.py`, import/use the parser and normalizer and implement `NoteIndex()`:
- `upsert(note_id, text, tags) -> None`: insert or replace a note. ID is a guaranteed
  nonempty string; text is a string; tags is an iterable of strings. Normalize and
  deduplicate tags; a bad tag raises `ValueError` without changing the old note or
  index. Copy input tags. Empty tags are allowed.
- `remove(note_id) -> None`: delete the note and all its tag memberships; missing
  ID raises `KeyError`.
- `search(query) -> list[tuple[str, str, tuple[str, ...]]]`: parse the query, require
  at least one tag from every positive group, and none of the excluded tags.
  With no positive groups start with all notes (including untagged notes).
  Return `(id, text, sorted_tags_tuple)` sorted lexically by ID. Unknown positive
  tags match nothing; unknown exclusions have no effect. Return a fresh list.
- `tag_counts() -> dict[str, int]`: count notes per normalized tag; omit tags with
  zero memberships, including after replacements/removals. Return a fresh dict.
Maintain a tag-to-note-ID inverted index and update it on replacement/removal.
